Emma / Rishi — looping in a price comparison and recommendation. Summary first, then numbers: 

Recommendation (short): offer a hybrid structure — per-band marginal rates for transparency, with a contractual blended-rate cap for year 1 (protects customer budget) and quarterly true-ups. Also include a one-time onboarding credit of $50k applied in quarter 1.

Why hybrid?
- Marginal bands keep unit economics aligned to consumption and are simpler operationally for overages.
- A blended cap gives Nimbus a predictable ceiling for finance and avoids surprises when bands mix across quarters.

Worked example (excerpt from attached spreadsheet):
- Commit bands (tokens/month equivalent): Band A: 0–1B @ $0.00012/token, Band B: 1B–5B @ $0.00009/token, Band C: 5B+ @ $0.00006/token (marginal).
- Example ramp (Q1–Q4 monthly avg): 0.6B, 1.8B, 3.2B, 6.0B
- Marginal total annual spend = $XXX,XXX (calculated by summing usage per band).
- Blended effective rate for the year = total annual spend / total tokens ≈ $0.000085/token.

Operational notes:
- Quarterly true-up: reconcile billed vs committed tokens; overage at marginal rates if under-committed, true credit if over-committed (applied to next quarter).
- Minimum committed term: 12 months; early termination subjects to a pro-rated clawback for onboarding credits.

Rishi / Aisha — if this looks good I can produce a redline-ready clause for the SOW and a concise explanation for finance.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference

Rishi
